provisions.title: Duties on receiving a correction request
provisions.text: (2) A Data Fiduciary shall, upon receiving a request for correction, completion or updating from a Data Principal,— (a) correct the inaccurate or misleading personal data; (b) complete the incomplete personal data; and (c) update the personal data.

provisions.title: Rights of Data Principals
provisions.text: (1) For enabling Data Principals to exercise their rights under the Act, the Data Fiduciary and, where applicable, the Consent Manager, shall prominently publish on its website or app, or both, as the case may be, — 30 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : EXTRAORDINARY [PART II—SEC. 3(i)]

provisions.title: Right to correction and erasure of personal data
provisions.text: (1) A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7, in accordance with any requirement or procedure under any law for the time being in force.

provisions.title: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
provisions.text: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

provisions.title: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
provisions.text: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

provisions.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
provisions.text: Every API endpoint that receives an ID of an object, and performs any action on the object, should implement object-level authorization checks. The checks should validate that the logged-in user has permissions to perform the requested action on the requested object.

provisions.title: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
provisions.text: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

provisions.title: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String
provisions.text: The web application uses an HTTP method to process a request, but the request includes sensitive information in the query string.

value.reason: The Evidence points to no working way for a user to correct their stored email address. The generic update route for the user record, PUT /api/Users/:id (server.ts:396-398), is blocked by security.denyAll(), so the auto-generated finale endpoint cannot be used to change a user's email. Email is taken at registration (POST /api/Users, server.ts:440-454) and written through the User model's email setter (models/user.ts:56-69). The only other self-service profile route is POST /profile (server.ts:707), handled by updateUserProfile. The part of that handler shown here only checks who is logged in and loads the user record; nothing shown reads req.body.email or passes email to user.update. This matches the positive example, where the profile route updates only username, rather than the negative one, which updates email. The other POST routes listed (profile image upload, Complaints, Recycles, Feedbacks) don't touch email. Caveat: the updateUserProfile excerpt is cut off before its update call, so this verdict relies on the blocked PUT route plus no email handling anywhere in the Evidence. Even so, the data flow shows email being collected, stored and exposed with no correction path, which falls short of the right to correct and update personal data.
